chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Hariz, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

There is no one possessing wealth of gold or silver who withholds its zakat, except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will detain him on the Day of Resurrection in a stony valley, and will send against him a hornless serpent that seeks him, while he flees from it. So when it sees that he has no escape from it, it will overpower him, seize him with its hand, and bite him as one bites a radish.
They shall have what they were niggardly of to cleave to their necks on the Day of Judgement

And this is the Word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. And there is no one possessing wealth of camels or sheep or cattle who withholds its zakat, except that Allah will detain him on the Day of Resurrection in a stony valley, wherein he will be trampled by every hoofed animal with its hooves, and torn by every toothed animal with its teeth.

And there is no one possessing wealth of dates or vines or crops who withholds its zakat, except that Allah will collar him with the produce of his land, stretching from the earth up to the seventh earth, until the Day of Resurrection.
ai.seo_question: What is the specific punishment in the afterlife for withholding zakat from gold, silver, livestock, or crops?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific eschatological retribution for withholding zakat, illustrating how the withheld wealth itself becomes the instrument of punishment: gold and silver transform into a biting serpent, livestock are trampled by their own kind, and agricultural produce becomes a collar extending to the seventh earth. The narration explicitly links these physical torments to the Quranic verse 3:180, emphasizing the concept of 'taqwa' (guarding) turning into a literal 'taqwa' (collar) of the withheld wealth, a theme deeply explored in Shia tafsir regarding the spiritual and material consequences of stinginess.
